title: Fixed-Rate Closing Interest Charge — Home Comfort Financing Statement Close
content:
On a Home Comfort Financing plan whose rate type is fixed, interest is posted once for each statement period as a closing interest charge on the first day after that period's statement closes.

The fixed-rate plans are the 60-Month 5.99% APR, the 120-Month 7.99% APR and the 144-Month 9.99% APR Fixed-Rate Plans. Statements close on the last day of the calendar month, so the closing interest charge for a statement period posts on the first day of the following month, and each closed statement period carries one closing interest charge, shown on the account as an interest line.

## Business effect at a glance

| Item | Effect |
|---|---|
| Accounts | fixed-rate Home Comfort Financing accounts |
| Frequency | once for each statement period |
| Posting day | the first day after the period's statement closes |
| On the account | an interest line on that month's statement; the balance rises by the charge |

## Posting the charge: `post_fixed_rate_interest_d84dbec7`

**Capability.** `post_fixed_rate_interest_d84dbec7` posts the closing interest charge on a fixed-rate Home Comfort Financing account for one closed statement month. The charge is added to the amount the borrower owes, appears on that month's statement as an interest line dated today, and the account balance rises by the same amount. The tool books the figure it receives.

**How it is invoked.** Agent-side: the agent unlocks `post_fixed_rate_interest_d84dbec7` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

1. `finance_account_id` — reference number of the fixed-rate financing account the interest is charged to, as shown by the financing account lookup for the verified borrower.
2. `statement_period` — the closed statement month the interest charge belongs to, written YYYY-MM (four-digit year, hyphen, two-digit month, e.g. 2026-04), in Eastern time.
3. `amount` — the interest charge to post, in USD, 2 decimal places, always positive, already rounded to the cent.

**Return.** The receipt carries `finance_txn_id` (reference number of the new interest line), `line_type` (always "interest"), `statement_period` (YYYY-MM month the charge was posted to), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD posting date), `account_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, the balance owed after the charge) and `status` — "posted" when the charge is on the account.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A call with `statement_period` 2026-08 and `amount` 47.28 on an account whose balance stood at $12000.00 returns `line_type` "interest", `amount` 47.28, `account_balance` 12047.28 and `status` "posted".
